## What this adds

This adds a `muse` provider so the SpecStory CLI can save and resume sessions from Muse Code, Meta's terminal coding agent. Muse Code stores each session as an event log at `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<session-id>/session.jsonl`. The store is not grouped by project. The provider reads the project folder from a record inside each transcript, the same way the codex provider does.

The full session format is documented in `docs/MUSE-FORMAT.md`. Every fact in that document came from running the muse binary and reading the files it wrote.

The provider covers the same commands as the claude and codex providers.

- `check`, `sync`, `list`, `watch`, `run`, and `reindex` all work.
- Resume works in both directions. We can rebuild another agent's session as a muse session, and muse resumes the file we write. We can also turn a muse session into another agent's native format.
- The common tools get dedicated markdown formatting. Shell results show their output and exit code instead of a raw JSON block. Edits render as a diff. Todo lists render as a checklist.

Three format details shaped the design.

- Muse writes subagent activity into the parent transcript under a different stream id, and it also writes a full separate transcript per subagent. The provider filters by stream id so subagent prompts never render as fake user turns, and it never treats a subagent transcript as its own session.
- The watcher only watches a trailing window of date folders, never the whole history. This follows the fix that stopped the codex provider from holding too many open files.
- Timestamps are microseconds and tool arguments are JSON strings. The provider converts both.

## How we tested it

Every command was run against sessions from the installed muse binary. We proved resume with a memory test. We wrote a session file ourselves, resumed it with muse, and muse answered a question that required memory of the earlier conversation.

We then ran a 12 agent verification workflow. Three agents drove muse through fresh scenarios in their own folders. Two agents audited the Go contracts and compared the markdown against claude output. A final pass tried to disprove every reported issue. Four of the five checkers passed with no issues. The confirmed findings were two small rendering fixes, and both are in this branch. `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run`, and `gofmt` are all clean.

## What is not fully tested

| Area | What works today | What is not verified yet |
|---|---|---|
| Resume picker | Rebuilding sessions is proven at the code level, and muse resumed a file we wrote. | Nobody has clicked through the interactive `specstory resume` picker with muse as the source or the target. |
| Cloud | Local sync works. | The cloud web app may not know the `muse` provider id yet. That change lives in the specstory-cloud repo, and it is small. Cloud display and cloud resume both wait on it. |
| Subagents, headless | Subagent records are correctly excluded, verified against a real interactive session. | We could not drive `subagent_spawn` in headless mode in this environment, so that path was not exercised end to end. |
| Images | Text sessions parse and render correctly. | A session with an image has not been generated. An image would be dropped from the markdown today. |

+## 1. Key findings
+
+The premise "copied verbatim" is only two-thirds true. Byte-for-byte diffs of the extracted function bodies show three tiers:
+
+1. **Byte-identical (pure copy-paste):** `normalizeToolName`, `languageFromPath` (the trio's variant), `classifyCheckError`, `trackCheckSuccess`, `trackCheckFailure`. `canonicalizePath` and `dispatchSession` differ only by a variable name and the log prefix string.
+2. **Semantically drifted copies:** `stringValue` (droidcli handles `fmt.Stringer`, `[]byte`, `float32`, `int32`, `uint`, `uint64`; the other two silently drop those types), `renderJSONValue` (droidcli handles `[]byte` but has an escaping bug — see §2), `todoSymbol` (deepseektui trims whitespace, droidcli doesn't; antigravitycli doesn't have it at all), `formatDiffBlock` (antigravitycli uses `TrimSuffix` where the others use `TrimRight`, so multiple trailing newlines render differently), and `renderGenericJSON` (antigravitycli is structurally different: it filters agy-injected `toolAction`/`toolSummary` keys and uses `json.MarshalIndent` instead of the hand-rolled sorted emitter).

66		cmd.Stderr = &stderr

187		if err != nil {
188			return nil, err
189		}
190	
191		// The store is keyed by session id (the id IS the directory name), so a
192		// glob resolves the path without reading any transcript.
193		//
194		// The id alone does not establish ownership, though: the store is global, so
195		// the glob will just as happily find another project's session. Confirm the
196		// transcript names this project before converting it — conversion stamps the
197		// requested project onto the result, so returning an unchecked match would
198		// file one project's conversation under another. The scan below applies the
199		// same rule via findMuseSessions.
200		directPath, err := findMuseSessionPathByID(sessionID)
201		if err != nil {
202			return nil, err
203		}
204		if directPath != "" && sessionFileBelongsToProject(directPath, projectPath) {
205			if chatSession := parseAndConvert(directPath, projectPath, debugRaw); chatSession != nil {
206				return chatSession, nil
207			}
208		}
209	
210		// Fall back to a scan: the id may name a session recorded under a layout
211		// the glob does not cover.
212		files, err := findMuseSessions(projectPath)
213		if err != nil {
214			return nil, err
215		}
216		for _, file := range files {
217			if file.SessionID == sessionID {
218				return parseAndConvert(file.Path, projectPath, debugRaw), nil
219			}
220		}
221	
222		return nil, nil
223	}
224	
225	// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single session directly from its known
226	// native file path, skipping by-id discovery. Used by reindex (which already
227	// holds NativePath from enumeration) to keep resolving N sessions O(N).
228	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
229		session, err := ParseSessionFile(nativePath)
230		if err != nil {
231			return nil, err
232		}
233		if len(session.Events) == 0 {
234			return nil, nil
235		}
236		return convertToAgentChatSession(session, originCwd, debugRaw), nil
237	}
238	
239	// parseAndConvert parses one transcript and converts it, logging and returning
240	// nil for files that are unreadable or hold no conversation yet.
241	func parseAndConvert(filePath string, workspaceRoot string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
242		session, err := ParseSessionFile(filePath)
243		if err != nil {
244			slog.Warn("parseAndConvert: Failed to parse Muse session file, skipping",
245				"file", filePath, "error", err)
246			return nil
247		}
248		if len(session.Events) == 0 {
249			slog.Debug("parseAndConvert: Session file has no conversation events", "file", filePath)
250			return nil
251		}
252		return convertToAgentChatSession(session, workspaceRoot, debugRaw)
253	}
254	
255	// convertToAgentChatSession converts a MuseSession to the provider-agnostic
256	// AgentChatSession format. Used by both sync mode and watch mode.
257	func convertToAgentChatSession(session *MuseSession, workspaceRoot string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
258		sessionData, err := GenerateAgentSession(session, workspaceRoot)
259		if err != nil {
260			slog.Error("convertToAgentChatSession: failed to generate session data",
261				"sessionId", session.ID,
262				"error", err)
263			return nil
264		}
265	
266		slug := museSessionSlug(session)
267		sessionData.Slug = slug
268	
269		// Raw data: the original JSONL transcript
270		rawData, err := os.ReadFile(session.FilePath)
271		if err != nil {
272			slog.Debug("convertToAgentChatSession: failed to read raw transcript",
273				"path", session.FilePath, "error", err)
274			rawData = nil
275		}
276	
277		if debugRaw {
278			if err := writeDebugRawFiles(session); err != nil {
279				slog.Debug("convertToAgentChatSession: failed to write debug files",
280					"sessionId", session.ID,
281					"error", err)
282			}
283		}
284	
285		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
286			SessionID:   session.ID,
287			CreatedAt:   session.StartTime,
288			Slug:        slug,
289			SessionData: sessionData,
290			RawData:     string(rawData),
291		}
292	}
293	
294	// museSessionSlug derives the filename-safe slug from the prompt that opened
295	// the session.
296	func museSessionSlug(session *MuseSession) string {
297		if prompt := session.FirstUserPrompt(); prompt != "" {
298			if slug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(prompt); slug != "" {
299				return slug
300			}
301		}
302		return "muse-session"
303	}
304	
305	// writeDebugRawFiles writes debug JSON files for a Muse Code session.
306	// Each conversation event is written as a numbered JSON file in
307	// .specstory/debug/<session-id>/. Only conversation events are written: the
308	// telemetry and diagnostics records the parser drops are noise for debugging
309	// markdown generation.
310	func writeDebugRawFiles(session *MuseSession) error {
311		debugDir := spi.GetDebugDir(session.ID)
312		if err := os.MkdirAll(debugDir, 0o755); err != nil {
313			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create debug dir: %w", err)
314		}
315	
316		for idx := range session.Events {
317			number := idx + 1
318			data, err := json.MarshalIndent(session.Events[idx], "", "  ")
319			if err != nil {
320				slog.Debug("writeDebugRawFiles: failed to marshal", "index", number, "error", err)
321				continue
322			}
323	
324			filename := filepath.Join(debugDir, fmt.Sprintf("%d.json", number))
325			if err := os.WriteFile(filename, data, 0o644); err != nil {
326				slog.Debug("writeDebugRawFiles: failed to write", "index", number, "error", err)
327				continue
328			}
329		}
330		return nil
331	}

333	// ListAgentChatSessions retrieves lightweight session metadata without full conversion.
334	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
335		projectPath, err := defaultProjectPath(projectPath)
336		if err != nil {
337			return nil, err
338		}
339	
340		files, err := findMuseSessions(projectPath)
341		if err != nil {
342			return nil, err
343		}
344	
345		result := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(files))
346		for _, file := range files {
347			session, err := ParseSessionFile(file.Path)
348			if err != nil {

350					"file", file.Path, "error", err)
351				continue
352			}
353			metadata := extractMuseSessionMetadata(session)
354			if metadata == nil {
355				slog.Debug("ListAgentChatSessions: Skipping session with no user prompt", "sessionID", session.ID)
356				continue
357			}
358			result = append(result, *metadata)
359		}
360	
361		return result, nil
362	}

364	// extractMuseSessionMetadata extracts lightweight metadata from a Muse session.
365	// Returns nil if the session never received a user prompt (a session that
366	// crashed during startup, or a transcript holding only telemetry).
367	func extractMuseSessionMetadata(session *MuseSession) *spi.SessionMetadata {
368		firstPrompt := session.FirstUserPrompt()
369		if firstPrompt == "" {
370			return nil
371		}
372	
373		slug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(firstPrompt)
374		if slug == "" {
375			slug = "muse-session"
376		}
377	
378		return &spi.SessionMetadata{
379			SessionID: session.ID,
380			CreatedAt: session.StartTime,
381			Slug:      slug,
382			Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(firstPrompt),
383		}
384	}

386	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every session in this provider's native
387	// store, regardless of project. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
388	//
389	// Muse's store is global and date-sharded, so the project association comes
390	// from the workspace_root recorded inside each transcript rather than from the
391	// path.
392	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
393		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)
394	}
395	
396	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates all sessions while reporting
397	// scan progress into r (nil-safe). Used by `specstory reindex`.
398	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
399		sessionsRoot, err := GetMuseSessionsDir()
400		if err != nil {
401			return nil, err
402		}
403		if _, err := os.Stat(sessionsRoot); err != nil {
404			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
405				return []spi.GlobalSessionRef{}, nil
406			}
407			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read Muse sessions directory: %w", err)
408		}
409	
410		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(sessionsRoot, "muse", r, func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
411			// Only top-level <session-id>/session.jsonl files are sessions;
412			// subagent transcripts belong to their parent.
413			if filepath.Base(path) != sessionFileName || IsSubagentTranscript(path) {
414				return nil, nil
415			}
416	
417			session, err := ParseSessionFile(path)
418			if err != nil {
419				return nil, err
420			}
421			metadata := extractMuseSessionMetadata(session)
422			if metadata == nil {
423				return nil, nil // telemetry-only or prompt-less session
424			}
425	
426			return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
427				SessionID:  metadata.SessionID,
428				CreatedAt:  metadata.CreatedAt,
429				Slug:       metadata.Slug,
430				Name:       metadata.Name,
431				NativePath: path,
432				OriginCwd:  session.WorkspaceRoot,
433			}, nil
434		})
435	}

437	func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
438		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: Starting Muse Code", "project", projectPath)
439	
440		SetWatcherDebugRaw(debugRaw)
441		if err := WatchMuseProject(projectPath, sessionCallback); err != nil {
442			slog.Error("Failed to start watcher", "error", err)
443		}
444		defer StopWatcher()
445	
446		if resumeSessionID != "" {
447			slog.Info("Attempting to resume Muse Code session", "sessionId", resumeSessionID)
448		}
449	
450		return ExecuteMuse(customCommand, resumeSessionID)
451	}
452	
453	// WatchAgent watches for Muse Code agent activity and calls the callback with
454	// an AgentChatSession. Does NOT execute the agent - only watches for activity.
455	// Runs until error or context cancellation (blocks indefinitely).
456	func (p *Provider) WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
457		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Starting Muse Code activity monitoring",
458			"projectPath", projectPath,
459			"debugRaw", debugRaw)
460	
461		SetWatcherDebugRaw(debugRaw)
462	
463		if err := WatchMuseProject(projectPath, sessionCallback); err != nil {
464			slog.Error("WatchAgent: Failed to start Muse session watcher", "error", err)
465			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start watcher: %w", err)
466		}
467	
468		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Watcher started, blocking until context cancelled")
469		<-ctx.Done()
470	
471		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Context cancelled, stopping watcher")
472		StopWatcher()
473	
474		return ctx.Err()
475	}

199	// ParseSessionFile parses a single Muse Code session.jsonl transcript. Records
200	// are kept in file order: the log is append-only and append order is the true
201	// conversation order (`muse resume` appends more runs to the same file).
202	//
203	// Records whose stream id differs from the session's own are dropped. The
204	// session id is established by the first record carrying a stream id (the
205	// metadata record written at session open) and falls back to the directory
206	// name, which is the session id in Muse's store layout.
207	func ParseSessionFile(filePath string) (*MuseSession, error) {
208		slog.Debug("ParseSessionFile: Reading Muse session file", "path", filePath)
209	
210		file, err := os.Open(filePath)
211		if err != nil {
212			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open file: %w", err)
213		}
214		defer func() { _ = file.Close() }() // Read-only file; close errors not actionable
215	
216		// A size-bounded Scanner rather than a bufio.Reader: ReadString materializes
217		// a whole line before any length check can reject it, so one enormous line
218		// forces exactly the allocation such a check exists to prevent. Scanner
219		// grows only to maxReasonableLineSize and then reports bufio.ErrTooLong.
220		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(file)
221		scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, initialScanBuffer), maxReasonableLineSize)
222	
223		// The store lays sessions out as <session-id>/session.jsonl, so the
224		// directory name is the authoritative session id when it is present.
225		// Settling the id up front makes parsing immune to record order, which
226		// matters for a transcript truncated mid-subagent.
227		session := &MuseSession{FilePath: filePath, ID: storeSessionIDFromPath(filePath)}
228		lineNumber := 0
229		foreignStreamRecords := 0
230		// Records read before the session's own stream is known (only reachable
231		// when the path did not settle the id).
232		var pending []MuseRecord
233	
234		for scanner.Scan() {
235			lineNumber++
236			line := scanner.Text()
237			if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" {
238				continue
239			}
240	
241			var record MuseRecord
242			// Unmarshal from a copy of the line: record.Payload is a
243			// json.RawMessage that aliases its input, records outlive the loop
244			// iteration, and the scanner reuses its buffer on the next line.
245			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &record); err != nil {
246				// Log and skip corrupted lines rather than failing the entire parse:
247				// the file may be mid-write when the watcher fires.
248				slog.Warn("ParseSessionFile: Skipping corrupted JSONL line",
249					"file", filepath.Base(filePath),
250					"line", lineNumber,
251					"error", err)
252				continue
253			}
254	
255			// The session's own stream is identified from the metadata record when
256			// the path did not already settle it. Records that arrive before the
257			// stream is known are held back rather than used to guess it: a
258			// transcript truncated mid-subagent starts with task-stream records,
259			// and adopting the first one would filter out the whole real
260			// conversation that follows.
261			if session.ID == "" {
262				if record.PayloadType == payloadTypeMetadata && record.Stream.ID != "" {
263					session.ID = record.Stream.ID
264					foreignStreamRecords += len(flushPending(session, pending))
265					pending = nil
266				} else {
267					pending = append(pending, record)
268					continue
269				}
270			}
271	
272			// Only a record that positively names a different stream is foreign. A
273			// record with no stream envelope cannot be attributed elsewhere, so it
274			// stays with the session.
275			if record.Stream.ID != "" && record.Stream.ID != session.ID {
276				foreignStreamRecords++
277				continue
278			}
279	
280			accumulateRecord(session, &record)
281		}
282	
283		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
284			if errors.Is(err, bufio.ErrTooLong) {
285				return nil, fmt.Errorf("line %d exceeds the %d MB limit: refusing to process a potentially malformed transcript",
286					lineNumber+1, maxReasonableLineSize/mb)
287			}
288			return nil, fmt.Errorf("error reading line %d: %w", lineNumber+1, err)
289		}
290	
291		// Nothing settled the stream: fall back to the first record's stream id
292		// (transcripts kept outside the store layout, e.g. test fixtures), then to
293		// the filename stem. Held-back records are replayed against that choice.
294		if session.ID == "" {
295			for _, held := range pending {
296				if held.Stream.ID != "" {
297					session.ID = held.Stream.ID
298					break
299				}
300			}
301			if session.ID == "" {
302				session.ID = sessionIDFromPath(filePath)
303			}
304		}
305		if len(pending) > 0 {
306			foreignStreamRecords += len(flushPending(session, pending))
307		}
308	
309		slog.Debug("ParseSessionFile: Parsed Muse session",
310			"path", filePath,
311			"sessionId", session.ID,
312			"eventCount", len(session.Events),
313			"foreignStreamRecords", foreignStreamRecords)
314	
315		return session, nil
316	}
317	
318	// storeSessionIDFromPath returns the session id from the store layout
319	// (<session-id>/session.jsonl) when the containing directory is named like a
320	// session id. It returns empty for transcripts kept elsewhere (e.g. test
321	// fixtures in a testdata directory), leaving the id to be settled from the
322	// records themselves.
323	func storeSessionIDFromPath(filePath string) string {
324		dir := filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(filePath))
325		if isSessionID(dir) {
326			return dir
327		}
328		return ""
329	}
330	
331	// isSessionID reports whether s has the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 hex session id
332	// shape Muse uses for its session directories.
333	func isSessionID(s string) bool {
334		if len(s) != 36 {
335			return false
336		}
337		for i, r := range s {
338			switch i {
339			case 8, 13, 18, 23:
340				if r != '-' {
341					return false
342				}
343			default:
344				isHex := (r >= '0' && r <= '9') || (r >= 'a' && r <= 'f') || (r >= 'A' && r <= 'F')
345				if !isHex {
346					return false
347				}
348			}
349		}
350		return true
351	}
352	
353	// flushPending folds the held-back records that belong to the now-known
354	// session stream, returning the records it dropped as foreign.
355	func flushPending(session *MuseSession, pending []MuseRecord) []MuseRecord {
356		var foreign []MuseRecord
357		for i := range pending {
358			if pending[i].Stream.ID != "" && pending[i].Stream.ID != session.ID {
359				foreign = append(foreign, pending[i])
360				continue
361			}
362			accumulateRecord(session, &pending[i])
363		}
364		return foreign
365	}
366	
367	// sessionIDFromPath derives the session id from the store layout
368	// (<session-id>/session.jsonl), falling back to the filename stem for
369	// transcripts kept outside that layout.
370	func sessionIDFromPath(filePath string) string {
371		dir := filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(filePath))
372		if dir != "" && dir != "." && dir != string(filepath.Separator) {
373			return dir
374		}
375		return strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(filePath), ".jsonl")
376	}
377	
378	// accumulateRecord folds one in-stream record into the session: envelope
379	// timestamps always, metadata and conversation events by payload type.
380	func accumulateRecord(session *MuseSession, record *MuseRecord) {
381		timestamp := museTimeToISO(record.RecordedAt)
382		if timestamp != "" {
383			if session.StartTime == "" {
384				session.StartTime = timestamp
385			}
386			if timestamp > session.LastUpdated {
387				session.LastUpdated = timestamp
388			}
389		}
390	
391		switch record.PayloadType {
392		case payloadTypeMetadata:
393			accumulateMetadata(session, record)
394		case payloadTypeSession:
395			accumulateRunEvent(session, record, timestamp)
396		}
397	}
398	
399	// accumulateMetadata folds a runtime.session.metadata record into the session.
400	// Fields are first-write-wins because the runtime emits metadata more than once
401	// per session and the later copies can carry blanked-out values.
402	func accumulateMetadata(session *MuseSession, record *MuseRecord) {
403		var payload museMetadataPayload
404		if err := json.Unmarshal(record.Payload, &payload); err != nil {
405			slog.Warn("accumulateMetadata: Skipping unreadable metadata payload",
406				"file", filepath.Base(session.FilePath), "error", err)
407			return
408		}
409	
410		if session.WorkspaceRoot == "" {
411			session.WorkspaceRoot = payload.Record.WorkspaceRoot
412		}
413		if session.ProviderID == "" {
414			session.ProviderID = payload.Record.ProviderID
415		}
416		if session.ModelID == "" {
417			session.ModelID = payload.Record.ModelID
418		}
419		if session.Version == "" {
420			session.Version = payload.Record.Build.Semver
421		}
422	}
423	
424	// accumulateRunEvent appends a conversation-carrying run event. Task-kind
425	// payloads are execution bookkeeping ("opening meta model stream") and every
426	// other event kind is diagnostics, so both are dropped here rather than in the
427	// conversion.
428	func accumulateRunEvent(session *MuseSession, record *MuseRecord, timestamp string) {
429		var payload museRunPayload
430		if err := json.Unmarshal(record.Payload, &payload); err != nil {
431			slog.Warn("accumulateRunEvent: Skipping unreadable run payload",
432				"file", filepath.Base(session.FilePath), "error", err)
433			return
434		}
435		if payload.Kind != "run" {
436			return
437		}
438	
439		var event museEvent
440		if err := json.Unmarshal(payload.Event, &event); err != nil {
441			slog.Warn("accumulateRunEvent: Skipping unreadable run event",
442				"file", filepath.Base(session.FilePath), "runId", payload.RunID, "error", err)
443			return
444		}
445	
446		switch event.Kind {
447		case eventStarted, eventReasoningCommitted, eventAssistantMessageCommitted,
448			eventAssistantToolCallsCommitted, eventToolResultBatchCommitted,
449			eventModelCompleted, eventTerminal:
450			session.Events = append(session.Events, MuseConversationEvent{
451				RecordID:  record.ID,
452				RunID:     payload.RunID,
453				Timestamp: timestamp,
454				Event:     event,
455			})
456		}
457	}
458	
459	// FirstUserPrompt returns the prompt that opened the first run, used for slugs
460	// and readable names.
461	func (s *MuseSession) FirstUserPrompt() string {
462		for i := range s.Events {
463			event := &s.Events[i]
464			if event.Kind() != eventStarted {
465				continue
466			}
467			if prompt := strings.TrimSpace(event.Event.Prompt); prompt != "" {
468				return prompt
469			}
470		}
471		return ""
472	}

80	// collectToolOutcomes gathers every tool result text keyed by tool call id, so
81	// tool messages can be built with their outputs folded in: results arrive in a

83	func collectToolOutcomes(events []MuseConversationEvent) map[string]string {
84		outcomes := make(map[string]string)
85		for i := range events {

87			if event.Kind() != eventToolResultBatchCommitted {
88				continue

96		}
97		return outcomes

100	// buildExchanges groups Muse run events into exchanges: one exchange per run,
101	// opened by `started` and closed by `terminal`.
102	func buildExchanges(events []MuseConversationEvent, defaultModel, workspaceRoot string) []Exchange {
103		outcomes := collectToolOutcomes(events)
104	
105		var exchanges []Exchange
106		var current *Exchange
107		var pendingUsage *Usage
108		model := defaultModel
109	
110		flush := func() {
111			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
112				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
113			}
114			current = nil
115			pendingUsage = nil
116		}
117	
118		// A transcript can begin mid-run (log rotation, truncation), leaving agent
119		// events with no `started` ahead of them; keep the turn rather than drop it.
120		ensureExchange := func(timestamp string) {
121			if current == nil {
122				current = &Exchange{StartTime: timestamp}
123			}
124		}
125	
126		// appendMessage carries over usage from a model step that reported before
127		// its output was committed (see attachUsage).
128		appendMessage := func(msg Message) {
129			if pendingUsage != nil {
130				msg.Usage = pendingUsage
131				pendingUsage = nil
132			}
133			current.Messages = append(current.Messages, msg)
134			current.EndTime = msg.Timestamp
135		}
136	
137		// attachUsage places one model step's usage on that step's own message.
138		// The runtime reports usage BEFORE committing tool calls but AFTER
139		// committing a final assistant message, so "the last message if it can
140		// still take usage, otherwise the next one" covers both orderings.
141		attachUsage := func(usage *Usage) {
142			if usage == nil || current == nil {
143				return
144			}
145			if len(current.Messages) > 0 {
146				last := &current.Messages[len(current.Messages)-1]
147				if last.Role == schema.RoleAgent && last.Usage == nil {
148					last.Usage = usage
149					return
150				}
151			}
152			pendingUsage = usage
153		}
154	
155		for i := range events {
156			event := &events[i]
157	
158			switch event.Kind() {
159			case eventStarted:
160				prompt := strings.TrimSpace(event.Event.Prompt)
161				if prompt == "" {
162					continue
163				}
164				flush()
165				current = &Exchange{
166					StartTime: event.Timestamp,
167					Messages: []Message{{
168						ID:        messageID(event),
169						Timestamp: event.Timestamp,
170						Role:      schema.RoleUser,
171						Content:   []ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: prompt}},
172					}},
173				}
174	
175			case eventReasoningCommitted:
176				// Reasoning is encrypted for the Meta provider, so text is usually
177				// empty; an empty thinking message would render as a blank block.
178				thinking := strings.TrimSpace(event.Event.Text)
179				if thinking == "" {
180					continue
181				}
182				ensureExchange(event.Timestamp)
183				appendMessage(Message{
184					ID:        messageID(event),
185					Timestamp: event.Timestamp,
186					Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
187					Model:     model,
188					Content:   []ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: thinking}},
189				})
190	
191			case eventAssistantMessageCommitted:
192				text := strings.TrimSpace(event.Event.Text)
193				if text == "" {
194					continue
195				}
196				ensureExchange(event.Timestamp)
197				appendMessage(Message{
198					ID:        messageID(event),
199					Timestamp: event.Timestamp,
200					Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
201					Model:     model,
202					Content:   []ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: text}},
203				})
204	
205			case eventAssistantToolCallsCommitted:
206				ensureExchange(event.Timestamp)
207				for j := range event.Event.ToolCalls {
208					appendMessage(buildToolMessage(event, &event.Event.ToolCalls[j], outcomes, model, workspaceRoot))
209				}
210	
211			case eventModelCompleted:
212				if event.Event.Model != "" {
213					model = event.Event.Model
214				}
215				attachUsage(convertUsage(&event.Event.Usage))
216	
217			case eventTerminal:
218				if current != nil {
219					current.EndTime = event.Timestamp
220				}
221			}
222		}
223	
224		flush()
225		return exchanges
226	}

242		// A malformed record can carry an empty tool name; fall back to a

244		// empty data-tool-name (matches the sibling providers' behavior).
245		name := call.Name

255			Output: buildToolOutput(outcomes[call.CallID]),
256		}
257	
258		return Message{

260			Timestamp: event.Timestamp,
261			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
262			Model:     model,

269	// the input map the schema expects. Anything that will not decode as an object
270	// is preserved verbatim so the markdown still shows what was requested.
271	func decodeToolArgs(args string) map[string]any {
272		if strings.TrimSpace(args) == "" {
273			return nil
274		}
275	
276		var input map[string]any
277		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args), &input); err != nil {
278			slog.Warn("decodeToolArgs: Tool args are not a JSON object, preserving raw", "error", err)
279			return map[string]any{"raw": args}

285	// reports failures as a "tool failed: <reason>" text rather than a status
286	// field, so the prefix is what separates an error from output.
287	func buildToolOutput(text string) map[string]any {
288		if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {

292			return map[string]any{"error": text}
293		}

302	// convertUsage converts one model step's token accounting to the shared Usage
303	// type. Muse splits cached input across cached_tokens and cache_read_tokens;
304	// both are input the model did not have to re-read, so they sum into
305	// CachedTokens. Returns nil when the step reported nothing.
306	func convertUsage(usage *MuseUsage) *Usage {
307		if usage == nil {
308			return nil
309		}
310	
311		converted := Usage{
312			InputTokens:   usage.InputTokens,
313			OutputTokens:  usage.OutputTokens,
314			CachedTokens:  usage.CachedTokens + usage.CacheReadTokens,
315			ThoughtTokens: usage.ReasoningTokens,
316		}
317		if converted == (Usage{}) {
318			return nil
319		}
320		return &converted
321	}

16	// formatToolAsMarkdown generates formatted markdown for a ToolInfo (input + output).
17	// Returns the inner content only (no <tool-use> tags - those are added by pkg/session).
18	// Also sets tool.Summary if a custom summary is needed.
19	func formatToolAsMarkdown(tool *ToolInfo) string {
20		if tool == nil {
21			return ""
22		}
23	
24		// Build custom summary for certain tools (appending key parameters)
25		var customSummary string
26		switch tool.Name {
27		case "read_file", "write_file", "edit_file":
28			if path := inputAsString(tool.Input, "path"); path != "" {
29				customSummary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, path)
30			}
31		case "search":
32			if pattern := inputAsString(tool.Input, "pattern"); pattern != "" {
33				customSummary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, pattern)
34			}
35		case "web_search":
36			if query := inputAsString(tool.Input, "query"); query != "" {
37				customSummary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, query)
38			}
39		}
40	
41		// Set custom summary on tool if we built one
42		if customSummary != "" {
43			tool.Summary = &customSummary
44		}
45	
46		// Build body content only (no wrapper tags)
47		body := strings.TrimSpace(formatToolBodyFromInput(tool))
48		result := strings.TrimSpace(formatToolResultFromOutput(tool))
49	
50		var builder strings.Builder
51		if body != "" {
52			builder.WriteString("\n")
53			builder.WriteString(body)
54		}
55		if result != "" {
56			// A single leading newline when there is no body: the wrapper already
57			// ends the <summary> line, so doubling here would stack blank lines.
58			if body != "" {
59				builder.WriteString("\n\n")
60			} else {
61				builder.WriteString("\n")
62			}
63			builder.WriteString(result)
64		}
65		if builder.Len() > 0 {
66			builder.WriteString("\n")
67		}
68	
69		return builder.String()
70	}

123		}

136		}
137		return builder.String()
138	}
139	
140	// formatShellResultFromOutput renders a bash result. The result text is a JSON
141	// object describing the run; showing just its `output` is what the user saw in
142	// the terminal, with the exit code called out when the command failed.
143	func formatShellResultFromOutput(output map[string]interface{}) string {
144		raw := outputAsString(output)
145		if raw == "" {
146			return ""
147		}
148	
149		var payload map[string]interface{}
150		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &payload); err != nil {
151			return addResultPrefix(formatOutputText(raw))
152		}
153	
154		// Backgrounded and PTY chunks report execution state instead of output;
155		// there is nothing better to show than the record itself.
156		text, ok := payload["output"].(string)
157		if !ok {
158			return addResultPrefix(formatOutputText(raw))
159		}
160	
161		var builder strings.Builder
162		if exitCode := schema.GetIntFromMap(payload, "exit_code"); exitCode != 0 {
163			fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "Exit code: %d\n\n", exitCode)
164		}
165		if trimmed := strings.TrimRight(text, "\n"); trimmed != "" {
166			builder.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("text", trimmed))
167		}
168		if builder.Len() == 0 {
169			return ""
170		}
171		return addResultPrefix(builder.String())
172	}
173	
174	func formatWriteFileBodyFromInput(input map[string]interface{}) string {
175		path := inputAsString(input, "path")
176		content := inputAsString(input, "content")
177		if path == "" && content == "" {
178			return ""
179		}
180	
181		var builder strings.Builder
182		if path != "" {
183			fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "Path: `%s`\n\n", path)
184		}
185		if content != "" {
186			builder.WriteString(spi.CodeFence(spi.LanguageFromPath(path), content))
187		}
188		return builder.String()
189	}
190	
191	// formatEditBodyFromInput renders an edit as a diff of its find/replace pair.
192	// Muse's own result text carries a mini diff too, but the inputs are what the
193	// model asked for and are present even when the edit failed.
194	func formatEditBodyFromInput(input map[string]interface{}) string {
195		path := inputAsString(input, "path")
196		find := inputAsString(input, "find")
197		replace := inputAsString(input, "replace")
198	
199		var builder strings.Builder
200		if path != "" {
201			fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "Path: `%s`\n\n", path)
202		}
203		if diff := diffFromFindReplace(find, replace); diff != "" {
204			builder.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("diff", truncate(diff, maxDiffRunes)))
205		}
206		return builder.String()
207	}
208	
209	// diffFromFindReplace renders a find/replace pair as diff-flavoured lines.
210	func diffFromFindReplace(find, replace string) string {
211		var builder strings.Builder
212	
213		writePrefixed := func(prefix, text string) {
214			if text == "" {
215				return
216			}
217			for _, line := range strings.Split(text, "\n") {
218				builder.WriteString(prefix)
219				builder.WriteString(line)
220				builder.WriteString("\n")
221			}
222		}
223	
224		writePrefixed("-", find)
225		writePrefixed("+", replace)
226	
227		return strings.TrimSuffix(builder.String(), "\n")
228	}
229	
230	// formatTodoBodyFromInput renders the todo list as a checklist. Muse todo items
231	// use "text" (Qwen uses "content", Gemini "description").
232	func formatTodoBodyFromInput(input map[string]interface{}) string {
233		todos, ok := input["todos"].([]interface{})
234		if !ok || len(todos) == 0 {
235			return ""
236		}
237	
238		var builder strings.Builder
239		builder.WriteString("Todo List:\n")
240		for _, raw := range todos {
241			todo, ok := raw.(map[string]interface{})
242			if !ok {
243				continue
244			}
245			text, _ := todo["text"].(string)
246			status, _ := todo["status"].(string)
247			fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "- [%s] %s\n", todoStatusSymbol(status), strings.TrimSpace(text))
248		}
249		return builder.String()
250	}
251	
252	func todoStatusSymbol(status string) string {
253		switch status {
254		case "completed":
255			return "x"
256		case "in_progress":
257			return "⚡"
258		default:
259			return " "
260		}
261	}
262	
263	// formatSubagentBodyFromInput shows what a spawned subagent was asked to do.
264	// The subagent's own transcript lives in a separate file, so the objective plus
265	// the spawn result is all the parent session records about it.
266	func formatSubagentBodyFromInput(input map[string]interface{}) string {
267		role := inputAsString(input, "role")
268		objective := inputAsString(input, "objective")
269	
270		var builder strings.Builder
271		if role != "" {
272			fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "Role: `%s`\n\n", role)
273		}
274		if objective != "" {
275			builder.WriteString(objective)
276		}
277		return builder.String()
278	}
279	
280	// formatDefaultResultFromOutput builds result with "Result:" prefix
281	func formatDefaultResultFromOutput(output map[string]interface{}) string {
282		content := outputAsString(output)
283		if content == "" {
284			return ""
285		}
286		return addResultPrefix(formatOutputText(content))
287	}
288	
289	// formatOutputText wraps multi-line output in a code fence, leaves single-line as-is
290	func formatOutputText(output string) string {
291		if strings.Contains(output, "\n") {
292			return spi.CodeFence("text", output)
293		}
294		return output
295	}
296	
297	// addResultPrefix adds "Result:" or "Result:\n" depending on content format
298	func addResultPrefix(content string) string {
299		if strings.Contains(content, "\n") {
300			return fmt.Sprintf("Result:\n%s", content)
301		}
302		return fmt.Sprintf("Result: %s", content)
303	}
304	
305	// inputAsString extracts a string value from tool input. Muse serialises
306	// unset optional arguments as JSON null, which must read as absent rather
307	// than as the literal "null".
308	func inputAsString(input map[string]interface{}, key string) string {
309		if input == nil {
310			return ""
311		}
312		val, ok := input[key]
313		if !ok || val == nil {
314			return ""
315		}
316		switch v := val.(type) {
317		case string:
318			return v
319		case fmt.Stringer:
320			return v.String()
321		case []byte:
322			return string(v)
323		default:
324			bytes, err := json.Marshal(v)
325			if err != nil {
326				return fmt.Sprint(v)
327			}
328			return string(bytes)
329		}
330	}
331	
332	// outputAsString extracts the primary output string from tool output
333	func outputAsString(output map[string]interface{}) string {
334		if output == nil {
335			return ""
336		}
337		if out, ok := output["output"].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(out) != "" {
338			return strings.TrimSpace(out)
339		}
340		if errStr, ok := output["error"].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(errStr) != "" {
341			return strings.TrimSpace(errStr)
342		}
343		return ""
344	}
345	
346	// outputErrorString returns the failure text when the tool failed, empty otherwise.
347	func outputErrorString(output map[string]interface{}) string {
348		if output == nil {
349			return ""
350		}
351		if errStr, ok := output["error"].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(errStr) != "" {
352			return strings.TrimSpace(errStr)
353		}
354		return ""
355	}
356	
357	func truncate(text string, limit int) string {
358		if limit <= 0 {
359			return text
360		}
361		runes := []rune(text)
362		if len(runes) <= limit {
363			return text
364		}
365		return string(runes[:limit]) + "\n... (truncated)"
366	}

1	package musecode
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"fmt"
7		"io"
8		"io/fs"
9		"log/slog"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
16	)
17	
18	// Package-level variables for mocking in tests
19	var (
20		osUserHomeDir = os.UserHomeDir
21		osGetwd       = os.Getwd
22	)
23	
24	const (
25		// sessionFileName is the transcript inside every session directory.
26		sessionFileName = "session.jsonl"
27	
28		// subagentDirName holds one transcript per spawned subagent. Those are not
29		// independent sessions and must never be enumerated as such.
30		subagentDirName = "subagent"
31	
32		// maxHeaderBytes bounds how much of a transcript is read to find its
33		// workspace root. The metadata record is written at session open and is
34		// always the first line, so a small prefix answers the question without
35		// touching multi-megabyte transcripts.
36		maxHeaderBytes = 256 * 1024
37	)
38	
39	// museSessionFile is a discovered transcript plus the header fields needed to
40	// decide which project it belongs to, without parsing the whole file.
41	type museSessionFile struct {
42		Path          string
43		SessionID     string
44		WorkspaceRoot string
45	}
46	
47	// GetMuseSessionsDir returns the root of Muse Code's session store. Muse is an
48	// XDG-conformant application, so XDG_DATA_HOME wins when set and the store
49	// otherwise lives at ~/.local/share/muse/sessions.
50	func GetMuseSessionsDir() (string, error) {
51		if dataHome := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("XDG_DATA_HOME")); dataHome != "" {
52			return filepath.Join(dataHome, "muse", "sessions"), nil
53		}
54	
55		homeDir, err := osUserHomeDir()
56		if err != nil {
57			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get user home directory: %w", err)
58		}
59		return filepath.Join(homeDir, ".local", "share", "muse", "sessions"), nil
60	}
61	
62	// defaultProjectPath fills in an empty project path with the current working
63	// directory. Provider entry points call this once so the same resolved path is
64	// used both for matching sessions to the project and as the workspace root
65	// stamped into generated session data (stamping the raw empty string would fail
66	// schema validation and break path hint normalization).
67	func defaultProjectPath(projectPath string) (string, error) {
68		if projectPath != "" {
69			return projectPath, nil
70		}
71		cwd, err := osGetwd()
72		if err != nil {
73			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get current working directory: %w", err)
74		}
75		return cwd, nil
76	}
77	
78	// walkMuseSessionFiles calls visit for every top-level session transcript under
79	// the date-sharded store. Subagent directories are pruned outright: they hold
80	// full transcripts in the same format, so enumerating them would invent
81	// sessions the user never started.
82	func walkMuseSessionFiles(sessionsRoot string, visit func(path string)) error {
83		return filepath.WalkDir(sessionsRoot, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
84			if err != nil {
85				return nil // skip unreadable entries rather than abort the sweep
86			}
87			if d.IsDir() {
88				if d.Name() == subagentDirName {
89					return filepath.SkipDir
90				}
91				return nil
92			}
93			if d.Name() != sessionFileName {
94				return nil
95			}
96			visit(path)
97			return nil
98		})
99	}
100	
101	// IsSubagentTranscript reports whether a transcript path sits under a subagent
102	// directory. Subagent transcripts share the session format but belong to their
103	// parent session, so every enumeration path filters them out.
104	//
105	// Matching happens on the slash form so the shape of the path decides, not the
106	// platform: Windows accepts forward slashes too, and a path can arrive from a
107	// record written on another OS.
108	func IsSubagentTranscript(path string) bool {
109		return strings.Contains(filepath.ToSlash(path), "/"+subagentDirName+"/")
110	}
111	
112	// workspaceMatchesProject reports whether a transcript's recorded workspace
113	// root is the given project, which must already be canonicalized.
114	//
115	// A transcript that records no workspace root never matches. The store is
116	// global, so a session that cannot name its own project cannot be claimed by
117	// one: treating "unknown" as "mine" would let any project adopt it.
118	func workspaceMatchesProject(workspaceRoot string, canonicalProject string) bool {
119		return workspaceRoot != "" && spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(workspaceRoot) == canonicalProject
120	}
121	
122	// sessionFileBelongsToProject reports whether the transcript at path records
123	// this project as its workspace, reading only the file's bounded header rather
124	// than parsing it.
125	//
126	// The Muse store is global and keyed by session id alone, so possessing an id
127	// says nothing about which project the session belongs to. Callers that resolve
128	// a session by id must ask this before returning it, or a lookup made from one
129	// project will hand back another project's conversation.
130	func sessionFileBelongsToProject(path string, projectPath string) bool {
131		workspaceRoot, err := readSessionWorkspaceRoot(path)
132		if err != nil {
133			slog.Debug("sessionFileBelongsToProject: Skipping unreadable transcript",
134				"path", path, "error", err)
135			return false
136		}
137		return workspaceMatchesProject(workspaceRoot, spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(projectPath))
138	}
139	
140	// readSessionWorkspaceRoot reads just enough of a transcript to recover the
141	// workspace root recorded in its metadata record. Returns "" when the file
142	// carries no metadata (a transcript truncated before its first record).
143	func readSessionWorkspaceRoot(filePath string) (string, error) {
144		file, err := os.Open(filePath)
145		if err != nil {
146			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to open session file: %w", err)
147		}
148		defer func() { _ = file.Close() }() // Read-only file; close errors not actionable
149	
150		header := make([]byte, maxHeaderBytes)
151		n, err := io.ReadFull(file, header)
152		if err != nil && err != io.EOF && err != io.ErrUnexpectedEOF {
153			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to read session header: %w", err)
154		}
155	
156		// The final line of the prefix is usually cut mid-record; it fails to
157		// unmarshal and is skipped like any other unreadable line.
158		for _, line := range bytes.Split(header[:n], []byte("\n")) {
159			if len(bytes.TrimSpace(line)) == 0 {
160				continue
161			}
162	
163			var record MuseRecord
164			if err := json.Unmarshal(line, &record); err != nil {
165				continue
166			}
167			if record.PayloadType != payloadTypeMetadata {
168				continue
169			}
170	
171			var payload museMetadataPayload
172			if err := json.Unmarshal(record.Payload, &payload); err != nil {
173				continue
174			}
175			if payload.Record.WorkspaceRoot != "" {
176				return payload.Record.WorkspaceRoot, nil
177			}
178		}
179	
180		return "", nil
181	}
182	
183	// findMuseSessions returns the transcripts whose recorded workspace root is the
184	// given project. The store is global and date-sharded rather than project
185	// scoped, so project association can only come from inside each file.
186	// Results are ordered most recent first (the YYYY/MM/DD path sorts
187	// chronologically).
188	func findMuseSessions(projectPath string) ([]museSessionFile, error) {
189		projectPath, err := defaultProjectPath(projectPath)
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193	
194		sessionsRoot, err := GetMuseSessionsDir()
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil, err
197		}
198		if _, err := os.Stat(sessionsRoot); err != nil {
199			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
200				slog.Debug("findMuseSessions: Muse sessions directory does not exist", "sessionsRoot", sessionsRoot)
201				return nil, nil
202			}
203			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read Muse sessions directory %q: %w", sessionsRoot, err)
204		}
205	
206		targetRoot := spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(projectPath)
207	
208		var paths []string
209		if err := walkMuseSessionFiles(sessionsRoot, func(path string) {
210			paths = append(paths, path)
211		}); err != nil {
212			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to walk Muse sessions directory: %w", err)
213		}
214	
215		var matches []museSessionFile
216		for _, path := range paths {
217			workspaceRoot, err := readSessionWorkspaceRoot(path)
218			if err != nil {
219				slog.Debug("findMuseSessions: Skipping unreadable transcript", "path", path, "error", err)
220				continue
221			}
222			if !workspaceMatchesProject(workspaceRoot, targetRoot) {
223				continue
224			}
225			matches = append(matches, museSessionFile{
226				Path:          path,
227				SessionID:     sessionIDFromPath(path),
228				WorkspaceRoot: workspaceRoot,
229			})
230		}
231	
232		// Descending path order is descending date order, so the newest sessions
233		// come first without stat-ing every file.
234		sort.Slice(matches, func(i, j int) bool {
235			return matches[i].Path > matches[j].Path
236		})
237	
238		slog.Debug("findMuseSessions: Completed scan",
239			"sessionsRoot", sessionsRoot,
240			"projectPath", projectPath,
241			"transcripts", len(paths),
242			"matches", len(matches))
243	
244		return matches, nil
245	}
246	
247	// findMuseSessionPathByID locates a session directory by id without reading any
248	// transcript: the store is keyed by session id, so the id is a path component.
249	// Returns "" when no such session exists.
250	func findMuseSessionPathByID(sessionID string) (string, error) {
251		if sessionID == "" {
252			return "", nil
253		}
254	
255		sessionsRoot, err := GetMuseSessionsDir()
256		if err != nil {
257			return "", err
258		}
259	
260		// sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<session-id>/session.jsonl
261		pattern := filepath.Join(sessionsRoot, "*", "*", "*", sessionID, sessionFileName)
262		matches, err := filepath.Glob(pattern)
263		if err != nil {
264			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to search Muse sessions for %q: %w", sessionID, err)
265		}
266		if len(matches) == 0 {
267			return "", nil
268		}
269	
270		// A session id is unique; more than one match means the same id was
271		// re-shared across days, so take the most recent.
272		sort.Sort(sort.Reverse(sort.StringSlice(matches)))
273		return matches[0], nil
274	}

2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"log/slog"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"

10		"strings"

14		"github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify"
15		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
16	)
17	
18	var (
19		watcherCtx           context.Context
20		watcherCancel        context.CancelFunc
21		watcherWg            sync.WaitGroup
22		watcherCallback      func(*spi.AgentChatSession)
23		watcherMutex         sync.RWMutex
24		watcherDebugRaw      bool
25		watcherWorkspaceRoot string
26	)
27	
28	func init() {
29		watcherCtx, watcherCancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
30	}
31	
32	const (
33		// watchWindowDays is how many days of lookback before today stay under an
34		// active fsnotify watch; the window also includes today, so up to
35		// watchWindowDays+1 date directories are watched at once.
36		//
37		// Muse's store is global and date-sharded, exactly the shape that caused
38		// Codex's fd exhaustion (changelog v2.6.0): fsnotify's kqueue backend on
39		// macOS holds an open file descriptor for every file in a watched
40		// directory, so watching all history pins one fd per session ever
41		// recorded. The trailing window keeps fd usage flat while still
42		// live-streaming sessions that span midnight or were resumed outside
43		// SpecStory.
44		watchWindowDays = 7
45	
46		// watchRefreshInterval is how often the watched set is re-evaluated, which
47		// is what carries the watcher across a day rollover: the new day's
48		// directory is picked up and directories that aged out are released.
49		watchRefreshInterval = 10 * time.Minute
50	
51		// watchBootstrapInterval is the retry cadence used while the session store
52		// does not exist yet (Muse has never run on this machine). There is no
53		// directory to hang an fsnotify watch on until then.
54		watchBootstrapInterval = 5 * time.Second
55	)
56	
57	func SetWatcherCallback(callback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) {
58		watcherMutex.Lock()
59		defer watcherMutex.Unlock()
60		watcherCallback = callback
61	}
62	
63	func SetWatcherDebugRaw(debugRaw bool) {
64		watcherMutex.Lock()
65		defer watcherMutex.Unlock()
66		watcherDebugRaw = debugRaw
67	}
68	
69	func SetWatcherWorkspaceRoot(workspaceRoot string) {
70		watcherMutex.Lock()
71		defer watcherMutex.Unlock()
72		watcherWorkspaceRoot = workspaceRoot
73	}
74	
75	func getWatcherWorkspaceRoot() string {
76		watcherMutex.RLock()
77		defer watcherMutex.RUnlock()
78		return watcherWorkspaceRoot
79	}
80	
81	func getWatcherDebugRaw() bool {
82		watcherMutex.RLock()
83		defer watcherMutex.RUnlock()
84		return watcherDebugRaw
85	}
86	
87	// StopWatcher gracefully stops the watcher goroutine.
88	func StopWatcher() {
89		slog.Info("StopWatcher: Signaling Muse watcher to stop")
90		watcherCancel()
91		watcherWg.Wait()
92		slog.Info("StopWatcher: Muse watcher stopped")
93	}
94	
95	// WatchMuseProject watches Muse Code's session store for transcript changes
96	// belonging to projectPath. The store is global rather than project-scoped, so
97	// every change is attributed by reading the transcript's own workspace root.
98	func WatchMuseProject(projectPath string, callback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
99		// Default the path before recording it as the workspace root, so sessions
100		// converted by the watcher never carry an empty root.
101		projectPath, err := defaultProjectPath(projectPath)
102		if err != nil {
103			return err
104		}
105	
106		SetWatcherCallback(callback)
107		SetWatcherWorkspaceRoot(projectPath)
108	
109		sessionsRoot, err := GetMuseSessionsDir()
110		if err != nil {
111			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get muse sessions dir: %w", err)
112		}
113	
114		watcher, err := fsnotify.NewWatcher()
115		if err != nil {
116			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create file watcher: %w", err)
117		}
118	
119		set := &watchSet{watcher: watcher, sessionsRoot: sessionsRoot, watched: make(map[string]bool)}
120	
121		watcherWg.Add(1)
122		go func() {
123			defer watcherWg.Done()
124			defer func() {
125				if err := watcher.Close(); err != nil {
126					slog.Debug("Muse watcher: error closing watcher", "error", err)
127				}
128			}()
129	
130			set.refresh()
131	
132			timer := time.NewTimer(set.refreshInterval())
133			defer timer.Stop()
134	
135			slog.Info("Muse watcher: watching session store", "sessionsRoot", sessionsRoot)
136	
137			for {
138				select {
139				case <-watcherCtx.Done():
140					slog.Info("Muse watcher: context cancelled, stopping")
141					return
142	
143				case <-timer.C:
144					set.refresh()
145					timer.Reset(set.refreshInterval())
146	
147				case event, ok := <-watcher.Events:
148					if !ok {
149						return
150					}
151					set.handleEvent(event)
152	
153				case err, ok := <-watcher.Errors:
154					if !ok {
155						return
156					}
157					slog.Error("Muse watcher error", "error", err)
158				}
159			}
160		}()
161	
162		return nil
163	}
164	
165	// watchSet tracks the fsnotify watches currently held on the session store.
166	// Not synchronized: it is owned by the single watcher goroutine.
167	type watchSet struct {
168		watcher      *fsnotify.Watcher
169		sessionsRoot string
170		watched      map[string]bool
171	}
172	
173	// refreshInterval slows down once the store exists: the fast cadence only
174	// exists to notice a first-ever `muse` run promptly.
175	func (s *watchSet) refreshInterval() time.Duration {
176		if info, err := os.Stat(s.sessionsRoot); err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
177			return watchBootstrapInterval
178		}
179		return watchRefreshInterval
180	}
181	
182	// refresh brings the watched set in line with the trailing window: adds the
183	// directories that should be watched now, and releases the ones that aged out.
184	// Called at startup and on every tick, which is what carries the watcher across
185	// a day rollover.
186	func (s *watchSet) refresh() {
187		if info, err := os.Stat(s.sessionsRoot); err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
188			slog.Debug("Muse watcher: sessions root not present yet", "sessionsRoot", s.sessionsRoot)
189			return
190		}
191	
192		desired := desiredWatchDirs(s.sessionsRoot, time.Now())
193	
194		for dir := range desired {
195			s.addWatch(dir)
196		}
197		for dir := range s.watched {
198			if !desired[dir] {
199				s.removeWatch(dir)
200			}
201		}
202	}
203	
204	// desiredWatchDirs returns every directory that should carry a watch right now:
205	// the sessions root, the date directories inside the trailing window, and the
206	// session directories inside those days. Only directories that exist are
207	// returned, so the caller never tries to watch a day Muse has not created.
208	func desiredWatchDirs(sessionsRoot string, now time.Time) map[string]bool {
209		desired := map[string]bool{sessionsRoot: true}
210	
211		for offset := 0; offset <= watchWindowDays; offset++ {
212			date := now.AddDate(0, 0, -offset)
213			yearDir := filepath.Join(sessionsRoot, fmt.Sprintf("%04d", date.Year()))
214			monthDir := filepath.Join(yearDir, fmt.Sprintf("%02d", int(date.Month())))
215			dayDir := filepath.Join(monthDir, fmt.Sprintf("%02d", date.Day()))
216	
217			// Ancestors are watched too, so the day directory's creation is seen
218			// the moment Muse starts the first session of a new day/month/year.
219			for _, dir := range []string{yearDir, monthDir, dayDir} {
220				if info, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
221					desired[dir] = true
222				}
223			}
224	
225			entries, err := os.ReadDir(dayDir)
226			if err != nil {
227				continue
228			}
229			for _, entry := range entries {
230				// Session directories only; subagent transcripts live one level
231				// deeper and are never sessions of their own.
232				if entry.IsDir() && entry.Name() != subagentDirName {
233					desired[filepath.Join(dayDir, entry.Name())] = true
234				}
235			}
236		}
237	
238		return desired
239	}
240	
241	func (s *watchSet) addWatch(dir string) {
242		if s.watched[dir] {
243			return
244		}
245		if err := s.watcher.Add(dir); err != nil {
246			slog.Debug("Muse watcher: failed to add watch", "directory", dir, "error", err)
247			return
248		}
249		s.watched[dir] = true
250		slog.Debug("Muse watcher: added watch", "directory", dir)
251	}
252	
253	func (s *watchSet) removeWatch(dir string) {
254		if !s.watched[dir] {
255			return
256		}
257		// Removal can fail if the directory was deleted; the kernel already
258		// released its fds in that case, so just drop our bookkeeping.
259		if err := s.watcher.Remove(dir); err != nil {
260			slog.Debug("Muse watcher: failed to remove watch", "directory", dir, "error", err)
261		}
262		delete(s.watched, dir)
263		slog.Debug("Muse watcher: removed watch", "directory", dir)
264	}
265	
266	// handleEvent reacts to one fsnotify event: a new directory inside the window
267	// starts being watched immediately (so a session created seconds from now is
268	// live, not waiting for the next refresh), and a transcript write is converted
269	// and published.
270	func (s *watchSet) handleEvent(event fsnotify.Event) {
271		if !event.Has(fsnotify.Create) && !event.Has(fsnotify.Write) {
272			return
273		}
274	
275		if filepath.Base(event.Name) == sessionFileName {
276			if IsSubagentTranscript(event.Name) {
277				return
278			}
279			processSessionChange(event.Name)
280			return
281		}
282	
283		// Anything else is only interesting when it is a directory that belongs in
284		// the window: a new day directory, or a new session directory inside one.
285		if !event.Has(fsnotify.Create) {
286			return
287		}
288		if info, err := os.Stat(event.Name); err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
289			return
290		}
291		if filepath.Base(event.Name) == subagentDirName {
292			return
293		}
294		if !dirWithinWatchWindow(event.Name, s.sessionsRoot, watchWindowCutoff(time.Now())) {
295			return
296		}
297		s.addWatch(event.Name)
298		s.adoptExisting(event.Name)
299	}
300	
301	// adoptExisting reconciles a directory that appeared while the watcher was
302	// already running, picking up whatever Muse put inside it before the watch
303	// landed.
304	//
305	// fsnotify only reports what happens after a watch is added, and Muse creates a
306	// session by making the day directory, the session directory and the transcript
307	// in immediate succession. Adding a watch on the day directory is therefore too
308	// late for everything already inside it: the first session of a day would be
309	// invisible until the next refresh, by which point the transcript is fully
310	// written and emits no further events. Walking the new directory once on
311	// arrival is what makes that session show up.
312	func (s *watchSet) adoptExisting(dir string) {
313		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
314		if err != nil {
315			slog.Debug("Muse watcher: could not adopt new directory", "directory", dir, "error", err)
316			return
317		}
318	
319		for _, entry := range entries {
320			path := filepath.Join(dir, entry.Name())
321			switch {
322			case entry.IsDir():
323				// Subagent transcripts are never sessions of their own.
324				if entry.Name() == subagentDirName {
325					continue
326				}
327				s.addWatch(path)
328				s.adoptExisting(path)
329			case entry.Name() == sessionFileName:
330				if !IsSubagentTranscript(path) {
331					processSessionChange(path)
332				}
333			}
334		}
335	}
336	
337	// watchWindowCutoff returns the earliest date (local midnight) whose directory
338	// is still watched.
339	func watchWindowCutoff(now time.Time) time.Time {
340		year, month, day := now.AddDate(0, 0, -watchWindowDays).Date()
341		return time.Date(year, month, day, 0, 0, 0, 0, now.Location())
342	}
343	
344	// museDirDepth returns how deep a directory sits under the sessions root:
345	// 1 = year, 2 = month, 3 = day, 4 = session directory. 0 means the path is not
346	// part of the store layout (which includes anything inside a session, such as
347	// subagent/ and tool-outputs/).
348	func museDirDepth(path string, sessionsRoot string) int {
349		rel, err := filepath.Rel(sessionsRoot, path)
350		if err != nil || rel == "." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, "..") {
351			return 0
352		}
353		parts := strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(rel), "/")
354		if len(parts) > 4 {
355			return 0
356		}
357		return len(parts)
358	}
359	
360	// dirWithinWatchWindow reports whether a store directory could hold sessions
361	// dated on or after cutoff, and therefore deserves an fsnotify watch. A session
362	// directory inherits the date of the day directory holding it.
363	func dirWithinWatchWindow(path string, sessionsRoot string, cutoff time.Time) bool {
364		depth := museDirDepth(path, sessionsRoot)
365		if depth == 0 {
366			return false
367		}
368	
369		rel, err := filepath.Rel(sessionsRoot, path)
370		if err != nil {
371			return false
372		}
373		parts := strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(rel), "/")
374	
375		year, err := strconv.Atoi(parts[0])
376		if err != nil {
377			return false
378		}
379		if depth == 1 {
380			return year >= cutoff.Year()
381		}
382	
383		month, err := strconv.Atoi(parts[1])
384		if err != nil || month < 1 || month > 12 {
385			return false
386		}
387		if depth == 2 {
388			return year > cutoff.Year() || (year == cutoff.Year() && time.Month(month) >= cutoff.Month())
389		}
390	
391		day, err := strconv.Atoi(parts[2])
392		if err != nil {
393			return false
394		}
395		date := time.Date(year, time.Month(month), day, 0, 0, 0, 0, cutoff.Location())
396		// time.Date normalizes out-of-range values (Feb 30 becomes March 2); a
397		// round-trip mismatch means the components were not a real calendar date.
398		if date.Year() != year || date.Month() != time.Month(month) || date.Day() != day {
399			return false
400		}
401		return !date.Before(cutoff)
402	}
403	
404	// processSessionChange parses a changed transcript and publishes it, but only
405	// when it belongs to the project being watched: Muse's store is global, so a
406	// session for an unrelated project can land in the same directory.
407	func processSessionChange(filePath string) {
408		slog.Debug("processSessionChange: Detected Muse session file change", "file", filePath)
409	
410		session, err := ParseSessionFile(filePath)
411		if err != nil {
412			slog.Error("processSessionChange: Failed to parse session file", "file", filePath, "error", err)
413			return
414		}
415		if len(session.Events) == 0 {
416			slog.Debug("processSessionChange: Session file has no conversation events yet", "file", filePath)
417			return
418		}
419	
420		workspaceRoot := getWatcherWorkspaceRoot()
421		if session.WorkspaceRoot == "" || spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(session.WorkspaceRoot) != spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(workspaceRoot) {
422			slog.Debug("processSessionChange: Session belongs to another project, skipping",
423				"file", filePath, "sessionRoot", session.WorkspaceRoot, "watchedRoot", workspaceRoot)
424			return
425		}
426	
427		agentSession := convertToAgentChatSession(session, workspaceRoot, getWatcherDebugRaw())
428		triggerCallback(agentSession)
429	}
430	
431	// triggerCallback is a helper to call the watcher callback with proper locking.
432	//
433	// Delivery is synchronous so transcript changes reach the consumer in the order
434	// fsnotify reported them, but a panic in the consumer is contained here: it
435	// would otherwise unwind the fsnotify event goroutine and take down the whole
436	// process over one malformed session.
437	func triggerCallback(agentSession *spi.AgentChatSession) {
438		watcherMutex.RLock()
439		cb := watcherCallback
440		watcherMutex.RUnlock()
441	
442		if cb == nil || agentSession == nil {
443			return
444		}
445	
446		defer func() {
447			if r := recover(); r != nil {
448				slog.Error("muse: session callback panicked", "sessionId", agentSession.SessionID, "panic", r)
449			}
450		}()
451		cb(agentSession)
452	}
453

1	package musecode
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"log/slog"
7		"os"
8		"os/exec"
9		"slices"
10		"strings"
11	
12		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
13	)
14	
15	// Package-level variable for mocking in tests
16	var execLookPath = exec.LookPath
17	
18	// resumeSubcommand is how Muse Code continues a session: `muse resume <id>`,
19	// a subcommand rather than a flag (like Codex, unlike Qwen's --resume).
20	const resumeSubcommand = "resume"
21	
22	// getDefaultMuseCommand returns the default muse command. It checks for muse in PATH.
23	func getDefaultMuseCommand() string {
24		if _, err := execLookPath("muse"); err == nil {
25			slog.Info("Found Muse Code in PATH")
26			return "muse"
27		}
28		slog.Info("Muse Code not found in PATH, defaulting to 'muse'")
29		return "muse"
30	}
31	
32	// parseMuseCommand parses a custom command string into executable and arguments.
33	func parseMuseCommand(customCommand string) (string, []string) {
34		if customCommand != "" {
35			parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
36			if len(parts) > 0 {
37				return parts[0], parts[1:]
38			}
39		}
40		return getDefaultMuseCommand(), nil
41	}
42	
43	// ensureResumeArgs makes sure the command line carries `resume <id>`. A custom
44	// command that already names the resume subcommand keeps its position (the id
45	// is filled in after it when missing) rather than gaining a second one; any
46	// other custom subcommand is left alone and the resume pair is appended, which
47	// is the only thing that can be done without second-guessing the user.
48	func ensureResumeArgs(args []string, resumeSessionID string) []string {
49		if resumeSessionID == "" {
50			return args
51		}
52	
53		for i, arg := range args {
54			if arg != resumeSubcommand {
55				continue
56			}
57			// An id already follows the subcommand: nothing to add.
58			if i+1 < len(args) && strings.TrimSpace(args[i+1]) != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(args[i+1], "-") {
59				return args
60			}
61			// slices.Concat always allocates a new backing array, so the caller's
62			// slice is never mutated.
63			return slices.Concat(args[:i+1], []string{resumeSessionID}, args[i+1:])
64		}
65	
66		return slices.Concat(args, []string{resumeSubcommand, resumeSessionID})
67	}
68	
69	// ExecuteMuse runs the Muse Code CLI, optionally resuming an existing session.
70	func ExecuteMuse(customCommand string, resumeSessionID string) error {
71		museCmd, args := parseMuseCommand(customCommand)
72	
73		args = ensureResumeArgs(args, resumeSessionID)
74		if resumeSessionID != "" {
75			slog.Info("ExecuteMuse: Resuming Muse Code session", "sessionId", resumeSessionID, "args", args)
76		}
77	
78		cmd := exec.Command(museCmd, args...)
79	
80		// Interactive mode: connect to the user's terminal
81		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
82		cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
83		cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
84	
85		slog.Info("ExecuteMuse: Starting Muse Code process", "command", museCmd, "args", args)
86		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
87			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start muse: %w", err)
88		}
89	
90		slog.Info("ExecuteMuse: Waiting for Muse Code to exit")
91		if err := cmd.Wait(); err != nil {
92			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
93			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
94				exitCode := exitErr.ExitCode()
95				slog.Info("ExecuteMuse: Muse Code exited", "exitCode", exitCode)
96				os.Exit(exitCode)
97			}
98			return fmt.Errorf("muse execution failed: %w", err)
99		}
100	
101		slog.Info("ExecuteMuse: Muse Code exited normally", "exitCode", 0)
102		return nil
103	}

31	// ReconstructSession rebuilds a Muse Code native transcript from the neutral
32	// SessionData so `muse resume <id>` can continue the conversation.
33	//
34	// Muse stores a session as an append-only event log: a metadata record at
35	// session open, then run events keyed by run_id. Tool calls and thinking are
36	// already flattened into agent text by FlattenSessionData, so reconstruction
37	// emits only the three events a conversation needs — `started` for a user turn,
38	// `assistant_message_committed` for an agent turn, and `terminal` to close each
39	// run. See docs/SESSION-PORTABILITY.md and docs/MUSE-FORMAT.md.
40	func (p *Provider) ReconstructSession(data *schema.SessionData, opts spi.ReconstructOptions) (*spi.ReconstructedSession, error) {
41		turns, err := spi.PrepareTurns(data, opts)
42		if err != nil {

44		}

52		encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false)
53	
54		sequence := int64(0)
55		emit := func(payloadType string, payload map[string]any) error {
56			sequence++
57			record := map[string]any{
58				"schema_version":         1,
59				"id":                     uuid.NewString(),
60				"stream":                 map[string]any{"kind": "session", "id": newID},
61				"sequence":               sequence,
62				"recorded_at":            baseMicros + sequence*recordSpacing,
63				"record_type":            "event",
64				"durability":             "durable",
65				"causation_id":           nil,
66				"payload_type":           payloadType,
67				"payload_schema_version": 1,
68				"payload":                payload,
69			}
70			if err := encoder.Encode(record); err != nil {
71				return fmt.Errorf("failed to encode muse record: %w", err)
72			}
73			return nil
74		}
75	
76		metadata := map[string]any{
77			"kind": "metadata",
78			"record": map[string]any{
79				"workspace_root":       workspaceRoot,
80				"provider_id":          "meta",
81				"build":                map[string]any{"semver": reconstructedSemver},
82				"tool_surface_version": reconstructedToolSurface,

84				// from, so the lineage stays traceable (matches claude/codex/qwen).
85				"specstorySourceSessionId": data.SessionID,

89			return nil, err
90		}
91	
92		currentRun := ""
93		closeRun := func() error {
94			if currentRun == "" {
95				return nil
96			}
97			err := emit(payloadTypeSession, museRunRecord(currentRun, map[string]any{
98				"kind":     eventTerminal,
99				"terminal": "completed",

41			t.Fatalf("failed to escape %q: %v", s, err)
42		}
43		return string(encoded[1 : len(encoded)-1])
44	}
45	
46	// writeSession copies a fixture into the store under datePath/sessionID,
47	// rewriting its workspace root. Returns the transcript path.
48	func writeSession(t *testing.T, sessionsRoot, datePath, sessionID, fixture, workspaceRoot string) string {
49		t.Helper()
50	
51		data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("testdata", fixture))
52		if err != nil {
53			t.Fatalf("failed to read fixture %s: %v", fixture, err)
54		}
55	
56		// The root is substituted into JSON string literals, where a Windows path's
57		// backslashes would otherwise read as escape characters and leave the
58		// fixture unparseable. Tool payloads carry a second layer of JSON encoding,
59		// so occurrences nested inside an escaped string need escaping twice; they
60		// are recognizable by their escaped surrounding quotes and rewritten first.
61		escaped := jsonEscape(t, workspaceRoot)
62		nested := jsonEscape(t, escaped)
63		content := strings.ReplaceAll(string(data), `\"`+fixtureWorkspaceRoot+`\"`, `\"`+nested+`\"`)
64		content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, fixtureWorkspaceRoot, escaped)
65	
66		dir := filepath.Join(sessionsRoot, filepath.FromSlash(datePath), sessionID)
67		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
68			t.Fatalf("failed to create session dir: %v", err)
69		}
70		path := filepath.Join(dir, sessionFileName)
71		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
72			t.Fatalf("failed to write session file: %v", err)
73		}
74		return path
75	}
76	
77	// writeFileFrom copies an existing file to dst, creating dst's parents.
78	func writeFileFrom(t *testing.T, src, dst string) {
79		t.Helper()
80	
81		content, err := os.ReadFile(src)
82		if err != nil {
83			t.Fatalf("failed to read %s: %v", src, err)
84		}
85		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755); err != nil {
86			t.Fatalf("failed to create %s: %v", filepath.Dir(dst), err)
87		}
88		if err := os.WriteFile(dst, content, 0o644); err != nil {
89			t.Fatalf("failed to write %s: %v", dst, err)
90		}
91	}

245	// The Muse store is global and keyed by session id alone, so a by-id lookup can
246	// reach any project's transcript. Returning one would not merely answer the
247	// wrong question: conversion stamps the requesting project onto the result, so
248	// the session would be filed under a project that never ran it.
249	func TestGetAgentChatSession_RejectsAnotherProjectsSession(t *testing.T) {

257		if err != nil {

259		}
260		if got != nil {
261			t.Errorf("project A was handed project B's session %q", got.SessionID)
262		}
263	
264		// The owning project must still resolve it, or the guard has simply broken
265		// by-id lookup instead of scoping it.
266		got, err = NewProvider().GetAgentChatSession(projectB, basicSessionID, false)
267		if err != nil {
268			t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
269		}
270		if got == nil {
271			t.Fatal("owning project could not resolve its own session")
272		}
273		if got.SessionID != basicSessionID {
274			t.Errorf("SessionID = %q, want %q", got.SessionID, basicSessionID)

227	// immediate succession, so by the time the watcher adds a watch on the new day

121	func TestReconstructSession_RecordEnvelope(t *testing.T) {
122		provider := NewProvider()
123		workspaceRoot := t.TempDir()
124	
125		rec, err := provider.ReconstructSession(sourceSessionData(workspaceRoot), spi.ReconstructOptions{
126			WorkspaceRoot: workspaceRoot,
127		})
128		if err != nil {
129			t.Fatalf("ReconstructSession failed: %v", err)
130		}
131	
132		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(rec.Content)), "\n")
133		// metadata + (started + assistant + terminal) per turn pair + session.end.
134		if len(lines) != 8 {
135			t.Fatalf("record count = %d, want 8", len(lines))
136		}
137	
138		var previousSequence, previousRecordedAt int64
139		for i, line := range lines {
140			var record MuseRecord
141			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &record); err != nil {
142				t.Fatalf("record %d does not parse: %v", i, err)
143			}
144			if record.Stream.Kind != "session" || record.Stream.ID != rec.SessionID {
145				t.Errorf("record %d stream = %+v, want session/%s", i, record.Stream, rec.SessionID)
146			}
147			if record.RecordType != "event" {
148				t.Errorf("record %d record_type = %q, want event", i, record.RecordType)
149			}
150			if record.Sequence <= previousSequence {
151				t.Errorf("record %d sequence = %d, not monotonic after %d", i, record.Sequence, previousSequence)
152			}
153			if record.RecordedAt <= previousRecordedAt {
154				t.Errorf("record %d recorded_at = %d, not monotonic after %d", i, record.RecordedAt, previousRecordedAt)
155			}

}

// TodoSymbol maps a todo-list item status to the character rendered inside a
// markdown checkbox. Unknown statuses render as an unchecked box rather than
// being dropped, so an agent adding a new status never loses the item.
func TodoSymbol(status string) string {
	switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(status)) {
	case "completed", "done":
		return "x"

// and passes through. A path with no usable extension (Makefile, LICENSE)
// returns "", leaving the fence untagged rather than asserting plaintext, which

// CapRunes truncates s to at most max runes, marking the cut. Rune-based so a
// cap never splits a multi-byte character. Scans rune boundaries instead of
// converting to []rune, which would allocate O(len(s)) for exactly the
// oversized tool results this cap protects against.
func CapRunes(s string, max int) string {
	if len(s) <= max {
		return s // fast path: byte length bounds rune length
	}
	count := 0
	for i := range s {
		if count == max {
			return s[:i] + "\n… (output truncated)"
		}
		count++
	}
	return s // more bytes than max but fewer runes (multi-byte characters)
}
